title: Module quiz: Thinking, effort and speed

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An agent on Sonnet 5.5 runs at `xhigh` effort, and a developer adds `between_tools` to stop up-front thinking. The request fails. Which statement matches the module?

options.text: The option is valid on Sonnet 5.5 at any effort level
options.says: Ruled out because the mode "needs high effort or below".

options.text: Each option is valid alone, but the pair is refused
options.says: The page says "Each setting is valid alone, and the pair returns a 400".

options.text: The option exists only on Opus models, so any use fails
options.says: Ruled out because the table says "skips thinking up front is Sonnet only".

options.text: The option works only if a manual budget is also sent
options.says: Ruled out because the only budget rule is "A manual budget is at least 1,024", which has no link to this mode.

origin.section: The practice: thinking, effort and speed set correctly per model

questions.stem: A helpdesk bot prints replies live for agents and also runs overnight bulk jobs. Management wants the speed option on all of it. What does the module say?

options.text: It suits only the watched output, since batches exclude it
options.says: The page says "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API." and the speed gain is for output people watch.

options.text: It suits neither, since it only lowers time to first token
options.says: Ruled out because "Speed benefits are focused on output tokens per second (OTPS), not time to first token (TTFT)."

options.text: It suits neither, because only the cloud platforms offer it
options.says: Ruled out because fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".

options.text: It suits both, at the standard price for the bulk jobs
options.says: Ruled out because fast mode carries a premium and "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API."

origin.section: Fast mode: faster output, higher price

questions.stem: A shared helper serves three Claude models and must never emit a parameter that one of them rejects. What design does the practice use?

options.text: It derives each field from the chosen tier and refuses bad pairs
options.says: The practice "turns what an application wants into request parameters for one model" and raises an error for the invalid pairs.

options.text: It sends one body to every tier and retries whenever the API objects
options.says: Ruled out because the same sentence says it builds "request parameters for one model", not one shared body.

options.text: It picks the lowest common field and drops the rest silently
options.says: Ruled out because the page warns the API "silently disables thinking for that request", which a silent drop would hide.

options.text: It reads each field from the reply to an earlier call
options.says: Ruled out because "The rules are the tables of this module", not a reply.

origin.section: The practice: thinking, effort and speed set correctly per model

questions.stem: A cost-conscious team wants cheaper answers on Opus 5.5 without losing the cache of a long conversation. Which plan fits?

options.text: Switch to fast mode for the cached turns and standard for the rest
options.says: Ruled out because the table row "Speed setting (fast or standard)" shows system and messages invalidated.

options.text: Change the top-level effort on every second turn and restore it afterward
options.says: Ruled out because "always discards the cached messages".

options.text: Choose the effort level once, before the first turn, and keep it
options.says: The page says to choose once per conversation and put what varies after the cached prefix.

options.text: Disable thinking after the first answer to cut the output
options.says: Ruled out because "Changing the thinking mode or the effort" is on the invalidation list.
